title: and where you meant or
idea: Joining conditions with the wrong word flips the logic. 'and' needs both true; 'or' needs either.

exercises.prompt: Rule: weekend if day is Saturday OR Sunday. Code: if day == 'Saturday' and day == 'Sunday'. What is wrong?
options: 'and' can never be true here; it needs 'or'
exercises.explanation: A day cannot be both at once, so 'and' is never True. It should be 'or' — either day counts.

exercises.prompt: With the buggy 'and' version, how many days print 'Weekend'?
exercises.explanation: Zero — no single day equals both names, so the condition is always False.

exercises.prompt: 'and' is true only when BOTH sides are true.
exercises.explanation: True. If either side is false, 'and' is false. That is why two different equality tests can never both hold.

exercises.prompt: 'or' is true when AT LEAST ONE side is true.
exercises.explanation: True. 'or' needs only one side to hold, which fits 'Saturday or Sunday'.

exercises.prompt: Opposite bug: 'discount only if member AND age 60+.' Code uses 'or'. What goes wrong?
options: Non-members who are 60+ wrongly get the discount
exercises.explanation: 'or' lets a young member OR any 60-year-old get the discount, which is too generous. It needs 'and'.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'both conditions must hold'?
exercises.explanation: 'and' requires both sides true at once — the right choice for 'member AND 60+'.

exercises.prompt: Which word means 'either condition is enough'?
exercises.explanation: 'or' is satisfied by one side, matching 'Saturday or Sunday'.

exercises.prompt: Match the everyday phrase to the right joiner.
exercises.explanation: 'both/all' -> and; 'either/any' -> or. Reading the rule in words tells you which to use.
Use 'or' so either weekend day makes the condition true.

exercises.prompt: How do you catch an and/or bug by reasoning alone?
options: Translate the rule to words and see if 'both' or 'either' is meant
exercises.explanation: Read the rule in plain words: 'both' signals and, 'either' signals or. Then check the code matches.
